rows.name: enemy sprite layout table
rows.notes: PRG ROM table of 8x8 sprite tile ids (sprite pattern table $0000) used to compose each enemy's/sprite's metasprite. It is a data block between the enemy-routine code ending at CPU $E73B (JMP $EB64) and the numeric data starting at CPU $E842: prgRom 0x673E-0x6841 (CPU $E73E-$E841). Entries are variable-length runs of tile ids padded with $FC (transparent), grouped into the sprite form (a 2-wide metasprite row count), e.g. Goomba entry 0x6792-0x6797 = FC FC 70 71 72 73; the red Koopa run A5 A6 A7 A8 A9; koopa/green-shell runs 6E 6E 6F 6F, 6D 6D 6F 6F, 6F 6F 6E 6E; 0x6808-0x6841 holds $BF-$EE ids. GOOMBA ENTRY: the 4 body tile ids 70 71 72 73 sit at prgRom 0x6794-0x6797 (CPU $E794), read as the top row $70,$71 and bottom row $72,$73 of the Goomba's 2x2 body, bracketed by the two blank $FC fillers at 0x6792-0x6793. HOW FOUND (no reference imported): search_memory prgRom for the Goomba's tile ids in draw order, hex '70 71 72 73', returned a SINGLE hit at 0x6794 (and '72 73' a single hit at 0x6796); the surrounding bytes are the $FC-padded tile-id runs of the other enemies. The table has NO direct absolute operand anywhere in the 32 KiB PRG (searches for '94 E7', '92 E7', '8C E7' found nothing; the one '90 E7' at prgRom 0x6121 is a BCC operand, not a pointer), so the game reads it indirectly (the reader was not pinned down; a per-frame read trace on CPU $E794/$E790 saw no access, so the ROM bytes are read once at spawn/load, not redrawn from ROM each frame). PROOF (ledgered write + reset + re-reach + screenshot, all in hack eval-sheet2-c): write_memory prgRom 0x6794 = $65 (was $70; $65 is the round fireball/ball tile CHR $65, raw grid a filled ball) with the reason 'change the Goomba metasprite's top-left body tile id'; reset_emulator; pressed Start, waited ~1 s, pressed Start again and held Right ~130 frames to World 1-1's first Goomba. list_sprites then decoded the Goomba's 6-entry OAM group (palette 7, OAM slots 52-57) as tiles $FC,$FC,$71,$65,$73,$72 - i.e. CHR tile 101 ($65) now occupies the slot where CHR tile 112 ($70) sat in the unedited Goomba ($FC,$FC,$71,$70,$73,$72) - and the screenshot shows the Goomba at screen ~(122,185)-(137,208) drawn with that different tile. undo_edit (ledger seq 1) restored the byte to $70. This proves prgRom 0x6794 supplies the Goomba's upper body tile. Caveat on drawing order: the game reverses the tile order with OAM horizontal flips for a left-facing Goomba, but the table bytes are always 70 71 72 73.

rows.name: CHR origin of the Goomba top-left tile
rows.notes: The Goomba metasprite's top-left body tile is CHR $70 (tile 112) in the SPRITE pattern table $0000, so its 16 pixel-bytes live at CHR ROM offset 0x700 (1792). Metasprite table entry (prgRom 0x6794): FC FC 70 71 72 73, i.e. top row $70|$71 and bottom row $72|$73 bracketed by two blank $FC fillers. Because the 1-1 Goomba walks left, the engine emits the group reversed with OAM flip_h: list_sprites showed OAM indices 14/15 = tiles $71/$70 at screen x=124/132 and 16/17 = $73/$72 at x=124/132 (palette 7), so the table's upper-left tile $70 is the cell drawn at the Goomba's screen RIGHT (x=132) on a left-facing Goomba. PROOF (ledgered CHR-ROM write + reset + re-reach + screenshot, hack eval-sheet2-c): read_tile chrRom $70 gave the diagonal dome edge; write_tile target chrRom tile_id 112 with a bold peach/black concentric-square pattern (reason: prove the Goomba top-left tile lives at this CHR ROM offset) ledgered as edit #1 at chrRom offset 1792; read_memory chrRom 1792 len 16 returned the new bytes (00 7E 42 5A 5A 42 7E 00 FF 81 BD A5 A5 BD 81 FF); reset_emulator; played title Start/60/Start/120 then held Right 190 frames to 1-1's first Goomba; list_sprites again decoded the Goomba group with chr_tile 112 in the $70 slot, and get_pixel_color sampled the changed cell as $36 peach at (132,193)/(134,196) and $0F black at (133,194)/(138,198), matching the new pattern (palette 7 = $0F/$0F/$36/$17), while the neighbouring tiles $71-$73 kept their original art in the screenshot. undo_edit seq 1 restored the original 16 bytes (3,7,15,31,63,119,119,245,3,7,15,31,39,123,120,251). Found with no reference imported.
rows.why: after the ledgered write_tile to CHR ROM $700 (sprite table 0, tile $70) and a reset, the Goomba beside Mario shows the written pattern in its right top quarter, where a left-walking (h-flipped) Goomba draws $70; rom_origins chrRom 0x700, 16 bytes = table 0 * $1000 + $70 * 16
